title: Brunswick and Victor labels, early Ellington sides
summary: Braud and Allen sort out which early sides were on Brunswick or Victor, including Creole Love Call and Hop Head.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: That's the first date. Now that was the second date you just played there, because I remember this girl singing it. Bring Hand Breakdown, that was on the first date. That was Brunswick record, though. Oh, Brunswick, huh?
That's okay, this one. Was it okay or Brunswick? The one you played, was that?
So you made each single of Two Lovers and Bremen Hand Breakdown, just those two tunes, huh?
No, we made something else. I don't know how it's so long, but I don't remember. Yeah.
Did you ever make a tune called Hop Head?
No, not as I know of.

Yeah. Down in Our Alley Blues, did those come up? So Lova Queek? No. All right. Yeah, that's one of them. Well, you know, that's the way you come into the band earlier than I thought. You know, that's what I was asking, I got the book.
